title: Aussie Barbecue Haloumi Burgers
subtitle: with Sweet Potato Chips
description: Whether you're full-time vego or part-time only, our varied range of vegetarian dishes really hits the spot. Bursting with veggies, dairy, legumes, grains and nuts, they're packed with flavour, they’ll fill you up and they're totally mouth-watering too!

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Preheat the oven to 220C, fan-forced. Line an oven tray with baking paper. Cut the unpeeled sweet potato into 1cm-thick chips. Thinly slice the tomato and onion. Cut the haloumi into 1cm-thick slices. Combine half the barbecue seasoning and 3 tsp olive oil in a large bowl and season with salt and pepper. Add the haloumi and turn to coat.

Roast sweet potato chips: Put the sweet potato on the lined tray. Drizzle with 3 tsp olive oil, scatter over the remaining barbecue seasoning, season with salt and pepper and toss to coat. Roast, turning halfway, for 20-25 mins until golden and tender.

Caramelise onion: Meanwhile, heat 2 tsp olive oil in a medium frypan over medium heat. Cook the onion, stirring regularly, for 5 mins or until soft. Stir in 2 tsp red wine vinegar and 2 tsp sugar. Reduce the heat to low and cook, stirring occasionally, for 3-4 mins until caramelised. Remove from the pan and cover to keep warm. Wipe the pan clean.

Cook haloumi: Return the pan to medium-high heat. Cook the haloumi for 2 mins each side or until golden. Remove the pan from the heat. Meanwhile, cut the buns in half. Put on an oven tray, cut-side up, and bake for 5 mins or until toasted and golden.
Serve up: Spread the bun bases and tops with the mayonnaise. Layer the bases with the tomato, haloumi and caramelised onion. Sandwich with the bun tops and serve with the sweet potato chips. Enjoy!

Did you know?: Haloumi is a brined, slightly springy cheese originally from Cyprus. Traditionally it was made from a mixture of goat and sheep milk, although these days cow's milk is also used. The haloumi we use is made using vegetable rennet, so it's suitable for vegetarians.
